album.title: Radif of Persian Music on Setar I

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on C4 and dwells most on C in Owj (Oshshaq). Chaharpare (0:12.8) introduces Eb, centred on C. The line peaks at Eb4 (325.2 Hz) at 0:24.7. It closes on C3, not the tonic (Eb4 → C4 → C3 → C3 → C4 → C3).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic F set in the catalog (Bayat-e Esfahan's finalis F (182.3 Hz): three of the suite's five tracks voted it and the pitch set fits from it (0, 207, 293, 500, 705, 843, 1079 cents). The vote picked the 5th above (C): this track reads as Shur on C with F, its 4th, prominent, as Farhat describes Oshshaq (1990, p. 41). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 136.9 Hz (C)
